title: A vector of your own
description:
Write a small growing array to see what `std::vector` does inside.

```
push 1..10: capacity 1 2 4 8 16
size 10, capacity 16
reserve(100): capacity 100, data moved once
```
hints: `auto bigger{std::make_unique<T[]>(newCap)}; for (std::size_t i{0}; i < m_size; ++i) bigger[i] = std::move(m_data[i]); m_data = std::move(bigger);` (lesson 3.07).
This simple version needs `T` to be default-constructible; the real one uses raw memory and placement new.
requirements: Grow by doubling; move the old items into the new block.
Print each time the capacity changes.
